sources.name: Lowy · deep High Street window and small green box
sources.notes: Entire displayed architect photograph inspected natively. Deep pale perimeter and dark reveals enclose the long upper laboratory window; a separate small upper green box projects beside the service core. Exact offsets, panes and component heights are photo estimates. The brick Wallace Wurth in this historic photo predates its later redevelopment and is not restored in the model. No source pixels copied.

sources.name: Lowy · western shaded frame and recessed forecourt
sources.notes: Entire displayed courtyard photograph inspected natively. Separate green western frame contains closely spaced dark vertical shading, beside pale concrete core and a narrow glazed strip with projecting floor edges. Below it, glazing is recessed behind a round concrete post. Generated lower regions open this small forecourt; post, setback and frame dimensions remain reconstructed. Original mapped upper outline and height are retained.

sources.name: Lowy · February 2022 tapered plinth and paving
sources.notes: Official Street View at 34 High Street, -33.9164006, 151.2351776, inspected natively; visible capture date February 2022. Shows sloping west-end concrete underside, recessed lower wall, long pale beam, louvre strips, paving and mature planted verge. Beam level estimated at 5.1 m above the DEM-derived model base; 1.15 m setback and taper extent are also photo-fitted, not surveyed. Fine paving follows shared rendering / walking triangles and excludes original paths and tree bases. Historical appearance only.

additionalEvidence.observed: Entire displayed detail inspected natively: rough precast, faint panel joints, tie holes and small dark building lettering. Only original procedural concrete and building-name text used; institutional logos and source pixels are not copied.

Northern architect elevation previously inspected in the preceding pass. Corroborates tall service slots, projecting long window, small green box, lower recess and tapered end; unlabelled fine dimensions remain estimates.

reconstruction.streetWall: Fourteen narrow service slots replace the previous repeated flat strips, with pale jambs and actual sloping louvre faces. Fine vertical panel joints and larger horizontal precast divisions remain approximate.
reconstruction.longWindow: Estimated span 28–86 percent along the retained north face; relative base levels 22.6–27.7 m, 0.28 m frame width, 1.45 m projection and 0.12 m glass offset. Deep dark sill/head reveals sit clear of adjoining frame faces to avoid coplanar flicker.
reconstruction.smallBox: Separate north-east green frame at relative 17.8–28.4 m, estimated 0.75 m projection, two pane rows. The current reconstructed Wallace Wurth is retained.
reconstruction.westernScreen: Separate western frame, dark vertical blades, green return panels and a narrow pale-framed core window replace the old generic green / concrete treatment. Recessed lower glazing and one photo-fitted round post are added below.
reconstruction.lowerBody: Two derived lower regions plus two recesses exactly partition the original main footprint. Upper main body retains the full footprint above estimated 5.1 m. North frontage set back 1.15 m; western underside slopes from 0 to 5.1 m over approximately 5.86 m. Original MEDICAL_PARTS arrays and raw map coordinates remain unchanged.
reconstruction.collision: Thirty-one lower colliders cover the derived lower body. 0.20 m-wide strips use the minimum exact underside level, conservatively below the sloping visible surface by at most about 0.175 m. Existing main/bridge roof levels and all six earlier bridge support centres remain unchanged. The added western support has estimated 0.24 m radius.
reconstruction.paving: Two photo-fitted paved areas exclude occupied lower ground, neighbouring source buildings, full original route ribbons and 0.70 m source-tree base cutouts. All 8,455 nondegenerate triangles supply both rendering and indexed walking height; vertex heights use the retained DEM plus 0.22 m. Raw DEM and source path geometry remain unchanged.
reconstruction.reflections: A separate static 512 px probe faces High Street for street glazing, avoiding the courtyard reflection used by other Lowy glazing. Reflections show the reconstructed campus, never downloaded photography.
reconstruction.views: Four new exterior map destinations: High Street laboratory window, tapered street plinth, western framed screen and High Street green box.

preserved.basis: Original OSM maximum height and level tag. New component dimensions and fine levels are photo-fitted, not replacement measured building heights.
preserved.unchanged: Raw building footprints / tags, source paths, terrain samples, tree inventory records, existing bridge supports and documented surrounding building levels.

validation.targeted: Thirteen Lowy / medical checks passed. They cover lower partitions, conservative collision slices, facade roles, source preservation, four arrivals, post support and exact paving-to-walking agreement.
validation.browser: Both new lower openings walked successfully in a native browser: 69 m cumulative movement including approaches and return, roughly 57.3–57.8 m elevation. No warnings or errors captured.
validation.numerics: Boolean union verification alone rounds collision coordinates to 0.1 micrometre to avoid a clipping sweep failure on near-collinear edges. Independent area totals and runtime geometry retain full precision. Zero-area triangulation remnants are omitted before generating walking/rendering triangles.
validation.fullSuite: All 418 campus tests passed. Final browser inspection confirms the frame reveals no longer have coplanar flicker.

limitations: Photograph dates are unverified except February 2022 Street View. Fine levels, exact facade fabrication, post position and paving extent remain estimates. Some smaller services, landscaping and current institutional signs remain incomplete. Detailed interior layouts are not represented.
